questions.question: Use add_marginal_bars in order to know How does stress level affect sleep duration across different BMI categories?

answer.value: Stress level has a clear negative relationship with sleep duration across all BMI categories. People with the lowest stress level (3) consistently get the most sleep, averaging around 8.1-8.4 hours regardless of BMI category. As stress increases to the highest level (8), sleep duration decreases significantly to around 5.9-6.1 hours. This pattern suggests that higher stress is associated with shorter sleep duration, and this relationship holds true across normal weight, overweight, and obese individuals alike.

key_insights: Lowest stress level (3) has longest sleep duration
Highest stress level (8) has shortest sleep duration
The negative relationship is consistent across all BMI categories
BMI category has less impact on sleep duration compared to stress level
